title: Sofacy_Fysbis_Backdoor_Investigation_ec9
description: Investigate the Sofacy Fysbis backdoor compromise on the target network.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The target network has been compromised by the Sofacy group using the Fysbis backdoor. Your task is to investigate the compromise, identify the malicious activity, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the `target` host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From there, you can investigate the compromised system and identify lateral movement to other hosts. Enter `start` to begin.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the `target` host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From there, you can investigate the compromised system and identify lateral movement to other hosts. Enter `start` to begin.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: The `target` host is exhibiting unusual network activity. Investigate the running services to identify any unauthorized or suspicious services. The service `systemkernelservicedefender.service` is known to be malicious and should be identified as suspicious.
levels.solution: Check the systemd services and look for any services that do not belong to standard system services. The service name `systemkernelservicedefender.service` should be identified as suspicious.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Consider investigating system services to identify any anomalies.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: The suspicious service identified in the previous task is persisting across reboots. Investigate how this service is being automatically started. The persistence mechanism is known to be the systemd timer `lab-checkin.timer`.
levels.solution: Check the systemd unit files and timers to identify the persistence mechanism. The persistence mechanism should be identified as a systemd timer `lab-checkin.timer` starting the service `systemkernelservicedefender.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Explore systemd timers to understand how services are scheduled.

levels.title: Identify Lateral Movement
levels.content: The attacker may have moved laterally to other hosts in the network. Investigate the `target` host to identify any evidence of lateral movement. The service `payload-transfer.service` is known to facilitate lateral movement to the `next-target` host.
levels.solution: Check the logs and systemd services for any evidence of file transfers or remote execution. The service name `payload-transfer.service` should be identified as evidence of lateral movement to the `next-target` host.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Review logs and services for signs of remote execution or file transfers.
